newsitem.title: FRANCE: IMS sees lower 96 net income, dividend.
newsitem.headline: IMS sees lower 96 net income, dividend.

text.p: International Metal Service, a specialty metal distribution unit of Usinor Sacilor, said on Thursday it expected to show a net income of 115 million francs for 1996 on estimated turnover of 2.8 billion francs.
This would compare with a net profit of 152 million francs on turnover of 2.839 billion francs in 1995.
IMS also said it planned to cut net dividend to 21 francs per share from 28 francs in 1995.
In a statement IMS said that with a comparable structure, turnover fell an estimated 11 percent between 1996 and 1995.
Since July 1, 1996, IMS integrated the Datec, Siau, Meteco and Devis companies.
"After record results in 1995, IMS showed in 1996 its ability to resist in a difficult European economic situation," it said.
"Estimated cash flow capacity for 1996 of 150 million francs and a weak net debt level of 100 million francs give IMS the means to pursue its development," the statement said.
Usinor has through its Aster unit a 59.4 percent stake in IMS.
